analysis: This PR is documentation-only. docs/reference/configuration.md head changes are limited to lines 5-7: the intro now says provider CLI and native-runtime variables, and coordinator, console and admin settings belong to the platform reference. The base-side removal at lines 81-99 deletes the retained Console UI section (NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables). docs/reference/provider-authorization.md changes the last-updated date and repoints the console onboarding copy link from a local path to an immutable darkbloom-platform URL. The supplied head text for configuration.md (the SSD cache keys, prefix-cache env vars, MiMo/Nemotron/Qwen4 controls, model-cache location and others) was not changed by the patch. I read it as context and it looks consistent with the existing threat model (T-041 prefix-cache posture, TB-011 App Attest gating). No code, key handling, attestation, encryption, authorization or default behavior changes. Removing the console UI documentation does not weaken any provider-side control, and console hosting is out of scope (platform-owned). Pinned platform links are immutable evidence snapshots and grant no trust. One limit: configuration.md is only partly supplied (the patch excerpt is truncated and the head is shown from line 313), so I cannot confirm that the deleted console section left no dangling references elsewhere. I do not see a security consequence from that gap. No threat-model update is needed.
